questions.q: What does Oracle publish that documents every Financials table and view?
options: Documentation only for views, never for base tables
Nothing official — only third-party blogs cover this
An Enterprise Data Model reference, with a page per table/view covering name, description, primary key, and columns
A single PDF with no column-level detail
questions.explain: Oracle's Enterprise Data Model for Financials, published at docs.oracle.com, gives a dedicated reference page for each table and view.

questions.q: Why does the release cycle matter when reading Oracle Fusion documentation?
options: Documentation is versioned per quarterly release, so comparing against a different release is worth checking if something looks off
Oracle Fusion only updates once every ten years
Table names change completely every quarter
It doesn't matter at all
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion Cloud updates quarterly, and documentation is published per release — core financial tables are very stable, but release mismatches are a reasonable first thing to check.

questions.q: What four things does a typical table reference page provide, in order?
options: Only the column list, nothing else
A list of every user who has queried the table
Only a list of reports that use the table
Table name/module, description, primary key, column list
questions.explain: A table's reference page gives the table name and owning module, a description, its primary key, and the full column list with types and descriptions.

questions.q: Why shouldn't you guess a column's meaning purely from its name?
options: Column names are always unique across the entire schema
Similarly-named columns on different tables, like "status," can mean subtly different things, so the description matters
Column names are randomly generated and carry no information
Because all columns are named identically across every table
questions.explain: A "status" column on an invoice header and a "status" column on a payment schedule can mean different things — the documented description resolves the ambiguity.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a base table and a view?
options: There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
A view always has more columns than a base table
A base table is where data is physically stored, while a view is a saved query built on top of one or more base tables, often read-only
Views can never be documented by Oracle
questions.explain: Base tables hold the physically stored data; views, including the ones behind many OTBI subject areas, pre-join or pre-filter that data for reporting convenience.
